biological.citation: SARS-CoV-2-Induced PAPOLG Contributes to Inflammation Response by Stabilizing NF-κB mRNA (PMID: 40607946)
biological.summary: PAPOLG was significantly upregulated in SARS-CoV-2-infected THP-1 macrophages. Knockdown of PAPOLG promoted NF-κB mRNA degradation and decreased TNF-α and IL-6 levels, while overexpression stabilized NF-κB mRNA and enhanced cytokine expression. PAPOLG contributes to inflammatory response by stabilizing NF-κB mRNA through alternative polyadenylation.

biological.citation: Comprehensive analysis of GSEC/miR-101-3p/SNX16/PAPOLG axis in hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 35482720)
biological.summary: PAPOLG was identified as a component of a competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) regulatory network axis (GSEC/miR-101-3p/SNX16/PAPOLG) associated with hepatocellular carcinoma prognosis. PAPOLG was highly expressed in HCC with poor prognosis and the axis was associated with macrophage polarization and immune infiltration.

biological.citation: Systematic analysis of the frequently amplified 2p15-p16.1 locus reveals PAPOLG as a potential proto-oncogene in follicular and transformed follicular lymphoma (PMID: 31410080)
biological.summary: Amplification of the 2p15-p16.1 locus is associated with increased PAPOLG transcription in transformed follicular lymphoma (tFL) cases. PAPOLG showed increased expression after histological transformation from follicular lymphoma and was significantly overexpressed in FL cases compared to normal B-cells, suggesting PAPOLG as a critical gene in transformation to tFL.
biological.significance: p<0.05 for PAPOLG overexpression in FL vs normal B-cells

biological.citation: A diet rich in high-glucoraphanin broccoli interacts with genotype to reduce discordance in plasma metabolite profiles by modulating mitochondrial function (PMID: 23964055)
biological.summary: Single nucleotide polymorphisms associated with the PAPOLG gene were identified as differentiating two discrete phenotypic responses to high-glucoraphanin broccoli diet intervention. PAPOLG genotype significantly affected plasma metabolic profiles, particularly lipid and amino acid metabolites, TCA cycle intermediates, and acylcarnitines.
biological.sample_size: Subjects randomly assigned to dietary intervention groups
biological.significance: PAPOLG genotype P<0.001; PAPOLG genotype × diet interaction P<0.001

biological.citation: Analysis of differentially expressed microRNAs in bovine mammary epithelial cells treated with lipoteichoic acid (PMID: 35997417)
biological.summary: PAPOLG was identified as a target gene of differentially expressed miRNAs (bta-miR-196a, bta-miR-2285aj-5p, bta-miR-143, bta-miR-2433, bta-miR-2284f, bta-miR-2368-3p) in bovine mammary epithelial cells treated with lipoteichoic acid. Target genes were enriched in MAPK signaling pathway, rheumatoid arthritis, and cancer pathways.

biological.citation: A combined blood based gene expression and plasma protein abundance signature for diagnosis of epithelial ovarian cancer (PMID: 23551967)
biological.summary: PAPOLG was identified as one of 13 genes in a leukocyte-derived immune response signature for epithelial ovarian cancer diagnosis. The combined gene expression and plasma protein biomarker panel including PAPOLG achieved high diagnostic accuracy with 97.8% sensitivity and 99.6% specificity.
biological.sample_size: 343 samples (90 healthy, 253 EOC patients); validation with 65 controls and 224 EOC patients

biological.citation: Oocyte quality and in vivo embryo survival after ovarian stimulation in nulliparous and multiparous rabbit does (PMID: 35724452)
biological.summary: PAPOL-G (PAPOLG) expression was significantly different among experimental groups comparing nulliparous and multiparous females under superovulation treatment. PAPOL-G expression changes were associated with oocyte maturation and competence acquisition, affecting in vivo embryo viability.
biological.significance: p<0.05 for PAPOL-G expression differences among groups

biological.citation: ASHG 2011 - Refining the 2p15-p16 Microdeletion Syndrome (R. Lozano, W. Wilcox)
biological.summary: PAPOLG was identified within the 2p15-p16.1 microdeletion region associated with developmental delay, microcephaly, and dysmorphic features. A 1.11 MB deletion including PAPOLG and other genes was detected in a patient with the 2p15-16.1 microdeletion syndrome, suggesting PAPOLG involvement in neurodevelopmental phenotypes.
biological.sample_size: 1 patient case; 6 total reported cases of 2p15-16.1 microdeletion
